decisive_items: polygonal to short spindle-shaped cells formed small nests and sheets within dilated sinusoids without encapsulation
tumor cells exhibited clear cell borders, high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, hyperchromatic nuclei, frequent mitotic figures, and sparse hepatocellular necrosis
local invasion into adjacent blood vessels was seen
response.rationale: Primitive basophilic polygonal/spindle hepatocyte-like cells in nests/sheets with vascular invasion and reticulin network in a 7-week-old rat are characteristic of hepatoblastoma; HCC is less likely at this age and lacks the primitive spindle/basophilic pattern, while sarcomas lack hepatocytic differentiation.

rejected.why: Non-specific; normal gross/labs do not establish a specific liver disease.
Benign lesion; contradicted by invasion and frequent mitoses.
Mesenchymal sarcoma pattern; lacks the hepatocytic nests and young-age hepatoblastoma features.
No support; invasion and mitoses indicate neoplasia, not hyperplasia.
Too generic; specific hepatoblastoma features are present.
No glandular/ductal differentiation; perilobular basophilic foci are not supportive.
Endothelial/vascular tumor; lacks hepatocytic morphology and the described reticulin pattern is not vascular.
Same as hemangiosarcoma; no endothelial-lined vascular channels are described.
Generic malignancy; a specific hepatoblastoma diagnosis is supported.
Benign; contradicted by invasion, mitoses, and basophilic foci.
